A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same invariance-based causal representation learning framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ISTAnt treatment-effect estimation experiments and synthetic nintervention experiments in Section 5, with implementation details in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains both original empirical studies in Section 5, with implementation details in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The framework's optimization requirement is tightened: Constraint 3.2 now requires each selected invariant encoding block to preserve its corresponding latent information, whereas v1 imposed sufficiency on the full encoding. The implemented V-REx and synthetic autoencoder/MMD objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ISTAnt under experiment and position sampling and the same three-variable synthetic nintervention scenario. The added ISTAnt illustrations introduce no new evaluated data or tasks.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain V-REx across invariance weights, including ERM at zero weight, and the same model-selection criteria. Revisions to the literature-summary table concern theoretical mappings, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated ISTAnt encoder changes from DINO in v1 Section 5.1 to DINOv2 in v2 Table 2. This is a reported model-setting revision; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or the earlier name was corrected. Sampling scenarios, metrics, regularization sweep and synthetic settings are retained.

E4.justification: The invariance-weight sensitivity study, model-selection comparison and synthetic test of identification without causal interventions are retained. The new causal diagram and grooming examples illustrate the existing benchmark rather than add analyses.

E5.justification: v2 Table 2 newly specifies the ISTAnt seed set as range(20). Both versions already report 20 ISTAnt runs with standard deviations and three independently sampled synthetic ninterventional densities; no increase in repetitions or new statistical test is reported.

E6.justification: The ISTAnt curves, uncertainty displays and selected-model markers match between v1 Figure 2 and v2 Figure 1. Synthetic R² results remain 0.863 ± 0.031 for z1, 0.872 ± 0.035 for z3 and 0.065 ± 0.017 for z2.

T1.justification: v2 strengthens Constraint 3.2 and updates Theorem 3.1's proof, rewrites Proposition 3.3's argument with both necessity and sufficiency directions, and extends the graph-identification derivation from additive-noise ground truth to post-nonlinear models. It also removes v1 Appendix B.1(e)'s temporal KL/entropy equivalence derivation and revises other regularizer derivations. These are substantive changes beyond relocating retained results.

C1.justification: The central unification, variable-versus-graph identification distinction and practical applicability claims remain. Claimed coverage decreases from 31 to 30 existing identification results; correspondingly, the summary table drops the Ahuja et al. (2024) Theorem 5 identification case.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly excludes auxiliary-variable/statistical-diversity proof techniques from direct coverage in Appendix D.7, clarifies conditioning on the previous timestep when discussing temporal independence, and adds an asymptotic-consistency qualification to the ecology discussion. Existing discrete-variable and finite-sample limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix F.1 and Table 2 add local ISTAnt details including the class token, activations, weighted binary cross-entropy, optimizer parameters and 15 training epochs, where v1 largely referred to Cadei et al. A new reproducibility statement supplies an example-notebook link. Existing head size, learning rate, batch size and synthetic implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Heinze-Deml et al. (2018), Gresele et al. (2020), Hyvarinen et al. (2019), Oquab et al. (2023) and Zhang et al. (2012). It newly positions the imperfect-intervention corollary as addressing an open conjecture, delineates excluded proof techniques and revises several literature-table mappings. The broad research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and explanations are extensively edited. Detailed preliminaries, identification granularity, graph identification, related-work treatments and extended concluding discussions move into reorganized appendices, while the main text gains a compact related-work overview and ethics and reproducibility statements.

P2.justification: v2 adds the schematic overview in Table 1, the ISTAnt settings table and two adapted benchmark illustrations. The extensive literature table is regrouped and reformatted, the identification diagram moves to the appendix, and the document adopts conference formatting. The empirical plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: The schematic overview, clearer organization and newly explicit ISTAnt settings and notebook pointer improve accessibility and reproducibility. The theoretical revisions are less clearly beneficial: the expanded Proposition 3.3 proof still assumes that identifying one block excludes its information from the complementary encoding. The evidence therefore supports a limited improvement in exposition and documentation, rather than a demonstrated resolution of the theoretical gaps.
